key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): arthralgia (4.7% vs 3.3% placebo), headache (4.3% vs 3.5%), fatigue (2.6% vs 1.1%), diarrhea, oropharyngeal pain, nausea, myalgia, injection site reactions, influenza, neutropenia, and tinea infections. Serious risks include suicidal ideation and behavior (including 4 completed suicides), serious infections (0.5% vs 0.2% placebo), fungal infections (2.4% vs 0.9%), and neutropenia (0.7%)

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (incidence \ge1%) were arthralgia, headache, fatigue, diarrhea, oropharyngeal pain, nausea, myalgia, injection site reactions, influenza, neutropenia, and tinea infections. (6)
Suicidal ideation and behavior, including 4 completed suicides, occurred in subjects treated with SILIQ in the psoriasis clinical trials.
In clinical trials, subjects treated with SILIQ had a higher rate of serious infections than subjects treated with placebo (0.5% versus 0.2%) and higher rates of fungal infections (2.4% versus 0.9%).
During the 12-week randomized treatment period, neutropenia occurred in 0.7% of subjects in the SILIQ group.

detail.text: WARNING: SUICIDAL IDEATION AND BEHAVIOR — Suicidal ideation and behavior, including completed suicides, have occurred in patients treated with SILIQ. Prior to prescribing, weigh potential risks and benefits in patients with a history of depression and/or suicidal ideation or behavior.

detail.text: SILIQ is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the SILIQ REMS Program, with elements to assure safe use (ETASU), because of the observed suicidal ideation and behavior in subjects treated with SILIQ

citations.quote: SILIQ is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the SILIQ REMS Program because of the observed suicidal ideation and behavior in subjects treated with SILIQ [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].

In accordance with section 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Siliq (brodalumab) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of observed suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB) in subjects treated with Siliq.

vote.text: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met July 19, 2016; on whether the overall benefit/risk profile is acceptable to support approval, the vote was A (Yes, with labeling alone) – 4 votes, B (Yes, but only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented) – 14 votes, C (No) – 0 votes; a majority considered that Siliq should be approved only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented

citations.quote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, met on July 19, 2016, at the FDA White Oak Campus to discuss the Siliq application.

VOTE: Is the overall benefit/risk profile of brodalumab acceptable to support approval for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

A. Yes, with labeling alone to manage the risks
B. Yes, but only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented
C. No
Vote Result: A – 4 votes B – 14 votes C – 0 votes
A majority considered that Siliq should be approved only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented (Response B).

summary.text: BLA 761032 for Siliq (brodalumab) was received November 16, 2015 and reviewed under Standard review classification (not a priority/accelerated pathway). Efficacy was based on three Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. Because of observed suicidal ideation and behavior, the drug carries a Boxed Warning and was approved only with a REMS with elements to assure safe use, following Advisory Committee discussion on July 19, 2016.

citations.quote: Priority or Standard	Standard
To support an efficacy claim for Siliq (brodalumab) for the treatment of psoriasis, the applicant submitted results from three Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials.

In accordance with section 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Siliq (brodalumab) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of observed suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB) in subjects treated with Siliq.
